hardinessNote: UK RHS H5 rating assumes good drainage; excess winter wet is a more serious hazard than cold. Shelter pots from winter rain.
visual: Spreading rosettes of fleshy grey-green rounded leaves, sometimes pink-flushed; slender runners form offsets. Mature rosettes send up pointed cones of cream to pale-yellow flowers, then die and are replaced by offsets.
pest: Occasional mealybugs; rot after prolonged wet.
aspect: East or West, sheltered; filtered light or partial shade.
soil: Open, gritty, sharply drained sand, gravel or alpine mix; wide pH tolerance.
soilWarning: Avoid heavy clay, stagnant moisture, persistent high humidity and winter rain.
water: Water modestly in active growth only after the surface dries. Keep much drier in winter.
prune: Remove spent rosettes after flowering; retain developing offsets.
toxicity: No well-documented major toxicity; do not eat.
cvs: Often sold as Orostachys 'Chinese Hat'; the RHS treats this as a synonym of O. iwarenge.
resilience: Drought tolerant and cold hardy in very free-draining conditions; winter wet sensitive.
uses: Alpine troughs, sheltered rock gardens, gravel displays and succulent pots.
rootSize: Shallow, fine roots with runners and offsets.
pollination: Small flowers are visited by insects; flowering rosettes are monocarpic.
uncertain: Height varies by growing conditions and flowering stage.

hardinessNote: RHS H4; shelter from cold drying winds. Often semi-evergreen in milder UK gardens.
visual: Arching, finely divided fronds unfurl coppery-pink to bronze before turning glossy green; a graceful dense fern for woodland planting.
pest: Usually few problems outdoors; occasional slugs on emerging fronds.
aspect: North, East or sheltered West; dappled to full shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moisture-retentive but draining loam, clay or sandy soil; flexible pH.
soilWarning: Dry exposed sunny sites cause scorching; avoid letting new plantings dry out.
water: Water regularly until established. Maintain moisture in hot spells; mulch annually with leaf mould.
prune: Remove tattered or old fronds in late winter before new croziers unfurl.
toxicity: Do not consume; fern identification is important before any foraging.
cvs: 'Squires Any' on the supplied label is not confirmed as a cultivar, so this profile covers the species only.
resilience: Tolerates shade and some drier shade once established; dislikes harsh exposed positions.
uses: Woodland gardens, shaded beds, underplanting, large shady pots.
rootSize: Compact fibrous roots arising from a short rhizome.
pollination: Does not flower or set seed; reproduces by spores.
uncertain: The words 'Squires Any' could indicate a grower or sales label rather than a cultivar.

hardinessNote: Not reliably winter hardy outside in the UK. Keep frost-free, ideally bright and cool, through winter.
visual: Low, broad rosette of slender arching succulent leaves, heavily coloured dark burgundy-purple to nearly black in strong light, with silver overtones and small red marginal teeth.
pest: Mealybugs, scale, occasional vine weevil in pots; root rot if saturated.
aspect: South or West in summer; move under cover for winter.
soil: Open, gritty cactus/succulent compost with excellent drainage.
soilWarning: Avoid standing water, cold wet compost and all hard frosts.
water: Water well during warm active growth, then allow mix to dry substantially; reduce strongly in winter.
prune: Remove dead basal leaves carefully; no routine clipping.
toxicity: Sap may irritate skin; toothed leaf margins may scratch. Keep away from curious pets and children.
cvs: Sometimes treated under Agave rather than hybrid genus × Mangave. 'Night Owl' is a named horticultural hybrid.
resilience: Very drought tolerant once established; tropical-looking summer patio plant; frost tender.
uses: Architectural patio pots, succulent collections, conservatories and summer displays.
rootSize: Moderately shallow succulent fibrous root system; requires excellent drainage.
pollination: Flowers uncommon in UK container culture; flowering depends on plant maturity.
uncertain: Exact mature size and floral performance differ by nursery.
Hardiness reported under USDA zones rather than a cultivar-specific RHS temperature band.

common: Ling Ling Jug Plant / Panda Face Ginger
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy outdoors in sheltered, moisture-retentive but well-drained shade.
visual: Low evergreen carpet of glossy heart- or arrow-shaped dark green leaves with occasional silvery marbling. Curious ground-level blackish three-lobed flowers with white centres resemble a panda face.
pest: Occasional slugs and snails; crown rot in persistently soggy pots.
aspect: North or East; protected shade or dappled woodland light.
soil: Moist, humus-rich but draining soil; acid, neutral or alkaline acceptable.
soilWarning: Avoid parched exposed ground or baking afternoon sun.
water: Keep evenly moist during establishment and prolonged drought; avoid stagnant water.
prune: Remove damaged leaves in late winter; little pruning needed.
toxicity: Do not ingest. Asarum relatives may contain toxic aristolochic acids; treat all parts as potentially harmful.
cvs: Asarum arifolium 'Ling Ling' is the RHS-listed cultivar.
resilience: Excellent winter hardiness; slow but persistent shaded ground cover with adequate moisture.
uses: Woodland planting, shady troughs, collector pots, path edges and under shrubs.
rootSize: Small rhizomatous, shallow roots that spread gradually.
pollination: Unusual ground-level flowers may attract small crawling insects.
uncertain: Cultivar-specific toxicity research is limited; precaution based on Asarum genus.

hardinessNote: RHS H5. Winter drainage matters, especially in heavy soils.
visual: Architectural rosettes of stiff evergreen sword leaves, dark green with a broad creamy-yellow central stripe, often rose-tinted in colder weather. Mature plants raise tall spikes of ivory bells.
pest: Occasional aphids on flowers, snails and fungal leaf spot.
aspect: South or East; open full sun.
soil: Sharply drained sandy or loamy soil; acid to alkaline tolerated.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged winter waterlogging, dense shade and crowding.
water: Water to establish, then only occasionally during extended drought.
prune: Remove dead leaves with gloves and cut spent flower stems near the base.
toxicity: Can irritate skin; sharp leaves pose mechanical injury risk. Harmful to dogs and cats if eaten.
cvs: RHS spelling is 'Color Guard' (rather than 'Colour Guard').
resilience: Drought, salt spray and wind tolerant once established; avoid winter wet.
uses: Gravel gardens, Mediterranean-style borders, seaside sites and large architectural pots.
rootSize: Strong, deepening fleshy roots and rhizomatous offsets.
pollination: Creamy bell flowers attract some insects; seed set may be sparse without specialist moth pollinators.
uncertain: Listed ultimate height includes tall flower spikes; leaf rosettes stay much lower.

hardinessNote: Series marketed as fully hardy; this is an approximate RHS band, not a verified cultivar-specific RHS rating.
visual: Robust, mound-forming hellebore with glossy divided evergreen leaves and abundant double, soft blush-pink winter flowers held above the foliage. Outer petals can mature to muted pink-green.
pest: Hellebore aphids, leaf spot, black death virus and occasional slugs.
aspect: North, East or sheltered West; partial shade.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, neutral to alkaline, moisture-retentive but drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid severe summer drying, standing water and exposed hot afternoon sun.
water: Keep evenly moist until established; water during extended dry spells, especially in containers.
prune: Remove old or diseased leaves in late winter, ideally as flower stems rise. Deadhead if seedlings are unwanted.
toxicity: All parts poisonous if eaten; sap can irritate skin. Wear gloves.
compliance: Named ViV selections may be subject to breeders’ rights; check propagation licensing.
cvs: Label 'ViV Vers' interpreted as ViV 'Vera'; confirm from plant tag if possible.
resilience: Cold hardy and long flowering, tolerant of moderate shade once established.
uses: Winter borders, under deciduous shrubs, woodland-style schemes, seasonal planters and cut flowers.
rootSize: Dense fibrous roots from a perennial crown; avoid repeated division.
pollination: Winter flowers can supply nectar and pollen to early bees; double flowers may restrict access.
uncertain: Original input 'ViV Vers' may represent a different ViV cultivar.
Species/hybrid placement for nursery stock is sometimes given as Helleborus orientalis or hybridus.
H6 is estimated rather than verified for this cultivar.

hardinessNote: Best in mild sheltered positions; may drop leaves or suffer stem damage in colder winters.
visual: Low, spreading abelia with slender arching stems, small glossy dark-green foliage and masses of white funnel-shaped flowers, often flushed soft pink, surrounded by persistent rosy sepals.
pest: Generally few pests; occasional aphids; stress or root issues on poorly drained soil.
aspect: South or West, sheltered and sunny.
soil: Fertile, moist but draining loam, chalk or sandy soil; broad pH tolerance.
soilWarning: Poor flowering in deep shade; avoid winter waterlogging and harsh exposed frost pockets.
water: Water regularly while establishing. Once mature, water in extended dry spells.
prune: Lightly shape in spring and remove dead or damaged growth; avoid heavy autumn cutting.
toxicity: No major toxicity usually reported; not for consumption.
cvs: Also listed as Abelia 'Prostrate White' or 'Snowdrift'; some taxonomy uses Linnaea × grandiflora.
resilience: Reasonably drought tolerant when established; prolonged flowering through summer into autumn.
uses: Low edging, sunny banks, front of borders, wildlife planting and large pots.
pollination: Nectar-rich flowers attractive to bees and other insects.
uncertain: Foliage persistence varies widely in UK winters.

hardinessNote: Described as very hardy by growers; cultivar-specific RHS numeric rating not verified.
visual: Evergreen hellebore with leathery glossy deep-green divided leaves and exceptionally bright double pure-white flowers with a subtle green or cream centre. Mature blooms age cream then green.
pest: Aphids, hellebore leaf spot, black death virus and slug damage.
aspect: North or East; partial to full shade, avoiding oppressive dry shade.
soil: Rich, moist but drained loam or improved clay; neutral to alkaline preferred.
soilWarning: Avoid stagnant wet soil and extreme summer drought.
water: Water in dry spells, especially while flowering in pots; never leave pots in water.
prune: Remove worn or infected old leaves as new flowers emerge; deadhead if required.
toxicity: Poisonous if swallowed; skin and eye irritant. Wear gloves.
compliance: ViV vegetatively propagated selections may be protected by breeders’ rights; verify before propagation.
cvs: ViV 'Amalia' in the Helleborus ViV series; sold as orientalis/hybridus by different nurseries.
resilience: Hardy and winter-blooming; performs well in a sheltered shaded border.
uses: Winter interest, shade borders, decorative patio planters and underplanting.
rootSize: Compact crown with substantial fibrous roots.
pollination: Early flowers may attract bees; double petals can limit nectar access.
uncertain: Exact bloom start depends on propagation schedule and weather.
Hybrid naming differs across trade sources.
H6 hardiness figure is an estimate.

hardinessNote: RHS H7, though pot roots can still be damaged by extremes when containers freeze hard.
visual: Graceful evergreen fountain of arching narrow dark-green blades edged in creamy yellow-white; small inconspicuous brown sedge flower spikes in summer.
pest: Generally pest and disease free; occasional rust or root problems if stressed.
aspect: East, South or West, preferably light shade in hot positions.
soil: Moist but drained loam, sandy or improved clay soil; tolerant of broad pH ranges.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged drought, severe waterlogging and harsh hot reflected sun.
water: Keep evenly moist when establishing and in pots. Once established, water during prolonged drought.
prune: Comb out dead blades in spring or trim lightly April–July if untidy; avoid autumn hard pruning.
toxicity: Not generally regarded as toxic; leaves are not edible produce.
cvs: RHS trade name Evercream, cultivar denomination 'Ficre' (EverColor series). Correct species spelling: oshimensis.
resilience: Very cold hardy, evergreen, adaptable to partial shade.
uses: Border edging, modern containers, shade-texture planting and groundcover.
uncertain: Retail mature size depends on pot size and growing conditions.

hardinessNote: RHS H5; young variegated foliage may burn in late frost or drying wind.
visual: Glossy evergreen shrub with narrow leaves, red to olive-green new growth outlined in pink, maturing slate-green with creamy-white irregular leaf margins; occasional spring creamy flowers and red berries.
pest: Photinia leaf spot, powdery mildew, fireblight and occasional vine weevil.
aspect: East, South or West; sun to light shade; some wind protection preferable.
soil: Fertile, moist but free-draining loam, sandy loam or improved clay; neutral to slightly acidic.
soilWarning: Waterlogged or very exposed cold positions can trigger leaf loss; avoid excessively limey conditions if yellowing develops.
water: Water regularly for first one to two seasons, then mainly during extended drought.
prune: Trim in late spring after the first flush to encourage variegated new growth; remove reverted all-green shoots promptly.
toxicity: Ornamental berries are not for eating; wear gloves when pruning. Avoid ingestion by pets.
cvs: RHS lists trade name 'Louise' and cultivar denomination 'Mclarlou'.
resilience: Evergreen screening and colourful new growth; moderate resilience in sheltered UK sites.
uses: Colourful screening, specimen shrubs, hedges and large containers when maintained.
rootSize: Woody, extensive fibrous lateral roots; allow space from paving and other shrubs.
stockForm: Variegated evergreen shrub or small tree.
pollination: Small spring flowers provide insect forage; berries may feed birds.
uncertain: Large ultimate RHS size contrasts with smaller dimensions on frequently trimmed retail stock.

hardinessNote: Established plants are hardy, but fresh leaves are easily damaged by late frost and drying winds.
visual: Elegant cascading Japanese maple with exceptionally finely cut, deeply lobed leaves in deep garnet-red to bronze-red, brightening in autumn. Umbrella-like weeping canopy.
pest: Aphids, vine weevil in containers, verticillium wilt and fungal dieback.
aspect: East or sheltered West; morning sun or dappled shade.
soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive but draining loam or improved clay; preferably slightly acidic to neutral.
soilWarning: Avoid exposed drying wind, midday scorch, prolonged drought and waterlogging.
water: Water thoroughly in dry spells; container plants need reliable summer moisture without standing in water.
prune: Minimal pruning in dormancy, ideally late autumn to midwinter; remove dead, crossing or damaged branches.
toxicity: Not usually considered a major poisonous garden plant; do not eat.
cvs: Often labelled Acer palmatum Dissectum 'Garnet'; RHS accepted cultivar is Acer palmatum 'Garnet' (Dissectum Group).
resilience: Hardy in sheltered sites but sensitive to leaf scorch and drying conditions.
uses: Japanese-style gardens, waterside focal points, sheltered courtyards and large pots.
rootSize: Wide-spreading, shallow, fine woody roots; avoid soil compaction.
pollination: Small spring flowers provide some insect forage; samaras follow.
uncertain: Many nursery-grown specimens are grafted and therefore mature height depends on graft height and training.

hardinessNote: RHS H6; new growth can still be frost-scorched after a cold spring snap.
visual: Dense evergreen shrub with strongly toothed, glossy leaves; bright red to purple-red foliage emerges on new shoots before becoming rich green. White flower clusters may be followed by red ornamental berries.
pest: Leaf spot, powdery mildew, fireblight and occasional honey fungus.
aspect: Any aspect with sufficient light; best red colour in sun to part shade.
soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive yet draining clay, loam, sand or chalk; broad pH tolerance.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently soggy soil; exposed cold winds can burn young leaves.
water: Water routinely until rooted in; established shrubs need additional water mainly during drought.
prune: Clip two or three times in growing season for compact hedges and repeated bright red growth; avoid late-autumn hard pruning.
toxicity: Red berries are ornamental and not for consumption; use gloves while pruning and avoid pet ingestion.
cvs: RHS lists 'Magical Volcano' as the trade designation for cultivar 'Kolmavoca'.
resilience: Vigorous, evergreen, cold-hardy screening plant; responds well to clipping.
uses: Hedging, privacy screens, evergreen mixed borders, focal shrubs and large pots.
rootSize: Branching fibrous woody root system with lateral spread.
pollination: White clustered flowers support generalist insect visitors; fruits may be taken by birds.
uncertain: Summer flower and berry production may be limited by repeated clipping.
